claim_natural: Humans use only 10% of their brain at any one time.

claim_formal.subject: Human brain
claim_formal.property: proportion of brain actively used at any given time
claim_formal.operator_note: The claim asserts that only 10% of the brain is in use at any one time. This is disproved when >= 3 authoritative neuroscience sources reject the claim, providing evidence that substantially more than 10% of the brain is active at any given time. 'Use' is interpreted as neuronal activity detectable by functional brain imaging (fMRI, PET scans) or inferred from lesion studies.

source.quote: the "10 percent myth" is so wrong it is almost laughable, says neurologist Barry Gordon at Johns Hopkins School of Medicine in Baltimore

B2.label: MIT McGovern Institute — the 10% claim is '100 percent a myth'

source.name: MIT McGovern Institute for Brain Research
source.quote: the idea that we use 10 percent of our brain is 100 percent a myth

extraction.quote_snippet: the idea that we use 10 percent of our brain is 100 percent a myth

B3.label: University of Washington Neuroscience — no scientific evidence for 10% claim

source.name: Neuroscience For Kids, University of Washington (Eric Chudler)
source.quote: There is no scientific evidence to suggest that we use only 10% of our brains

extraction.quote_snippet: There is no scientific evidence to suggest that we use only 10% of our brains

cross_checks.independence_note: Sources are from different institutions: Scientific American (quoting Johns Hopkins neurologist), MIT McGovern Institute, and University of Washington. No organizational, funding, or ideological overlap.

adversarial_checks.question: Is there any peer-reviewed neuroscience study that supports the claim that only 10% of the brain is active at any given time?
adversarial_checks.verification_performed: Searched for: '10 percent brain myth credible support evidence true', '10% brain use scientific evidence peer-reviewed'. Reviewed results from Scientific American, Psychology Today, Wikipedia, Association for Psychological Science, MIT McGovern Institute, Medical News Today, and University of Washington.
adversarial_checks.finding: No peer-reviewed neuroscience study was found supporting the 10% claim. Every neuroscience source consulted explicitly labels it a myth. Brain imaging studies (fMRI, PET) consistently show activity throughout the entire brain, even during sleep.

adversarial_checks.question: Could the 10% figure refer to the ratio of neurons to glial cells, making the claim technically true under a different interpretation?
adversarial_checks.verification_performed: Searched for: 'neurons 10 percent brain cells glial ratio'. Reviewed neuroscience sources on neuron-to-glia ratios.
adversarial_checks.finding: While roughly 10% of brain cells are neurons (the rest being glial cells), the claim says 'use only 10% of their brain,' which refers to brain regions being active, not cell-type ratios. Furthermore, glial cells are also functionally active — they support neuronal function, maintain homeostasis, and participate in signaling. The neuron/glia ratio does not support the claim as stated.

adversarial_checks.question: Could William James's original 1907 statement be interpreted as literal neuroscience supporting the 10% claim?
adversarial_checks.verification_performed: Searched for: 'William James 1907 energies of men 10 percent origin'. Reviewed MIT McGovern and Wikipedia articles on the myth's origins.
adversarial_checks.finding: William James wrote in 'The Energies of Men' (1907) that 'we are making use of only a small part of our possible mental and physical resources.' He was speaking metaphorically about human potential, not making a neuroscientific claim about brain activity percentages. He never stated 10%, and his work predates functional brain imaging by decades.
